title: Leaders in an Array problem
stepTitle: Solve Problems on Arrays [Easy -> Medium -> Hard]
category: Solve Problems on Arrays [Easy -> Medium -> Hard]
problemStatement: An element is a leader if it is greater than everything to its right. Return all leaders.
intuition: Leadership depends only on the suffix maximum, so scanning right to left answers every element in O(1).

approaches.title: Brute: compare with all right elements
Optimal: suffix maximum sweep
approaches.idea: Walk backwards keeping the max seen; reverse the result at the end.
approaches.dryRun:
a=[10,22,12,3,0,6]
6 > -inf leader
0 no
3 no
12 leader
22 leader
10 no -> [22,12,6]
approaches.whyWorks: The suffix maximum is exactly the quantity the definition compares against.

edgeCases: Last element is always a leader
commonMistakes: Forgetting to reverse the collected list
Using >= when the definition says strictly greater
followUps: Next greater element (#214) — the monotonic stack generalisation
interviewInsight: Recognising this as a suffix-max problem, not a stack problem, is the efficiency point.
